==== src/VerifySample.Tests/ModuleInitializer.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=EmailPreviewServices&min=EmailPreviewServices&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;

// Everything here runs once, when the test assembly loads, before any test.
public static class ModuleInitializer
{
    [ModuleInitializer]
    public static void Initialize()
    {
        // Initializes every Verify.* plugin the project references and has not initialized above.
        // Explicit calls come first so their parameters apply: a plugin can only be initialized once.
        VerifierSettings.InitializePlugins();
    }
}

==== src/VerifySample.Tests/Plugins/EmailPreviewServicesTests.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=EmailPreviewServices&min=EmailPreviewServices&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using VerifyTests.EmailPreviewServices;

// Verify.EmailPreviewServices: Renders an html email in real email clients through a preview service, one scrubbed webp per device.
// https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.EmailPreviewServices
// Note: The key can be passed directly with VerifyEmailPreviewServices.Initialize("ApiKey")
// instead of the environment variable; without either, initialization throws.
// Note: Rendering is slow: roughly twenty seconds for one device, and the call throws after six
// minutes.
// Note: The snapshots are webp, so VerifierSettings.UseSsimForPng() does not apply to them.
// Note: Listing the same device twice throws, and each preview is deleted from the service once it
// has been fetched.
// Note: Around fifty devices are available, from Outlook 2003 to current mobile clients, light and
// dark.
public class EmailPreviewServicesTests
{
    // Each device gives one webp snapshot, named after it, so a change to the email is reviewed
    // as what each client actually shows rather than as html.
    // The client's own chrome is cropped out per device, so a browser update does not fail a test.
    // Not run by default: calls a paid service over the network and takes about twenty seconds per
    // device.
    [Fact(Skip = "calls a paid service over the network and takes about twenty seconds per device.")]
    public async Task Preview()
    {
        var preview = new EmailPreview
        {
            Html = "<html><body><h1>Hello from Verify</h1></body></html>",
            Devices =
            [
                Device.Outlook2019,
                Device.iPhone13
            ]
        };

        await Verify(preview);
    }
}

==== interactions

Warning licence-required: EmailPreviewServices needs An EmailPreviewServices api key: EmailPreviewServices is a paid service. The key is read from the EmailPreviewServicesApiKey environment variable, or passed to Initialize, and the rendering happens over the network.
